title: Preparation of Intact Bovine Tail Intervertebral Discs for Organ Culture
protocol: Obtain whole bovine tail from local abattoir, preferably without skin.
Prepare sterile work station and instruments on cutting board under sterile laminar flow hood.
Moisten sterile gauze with 0.9% sodium chloride containing 55 mM sodium citrate for each well of the 6-well plate.
Dilute Betadine solution to a concentration of 1% using tap water in a basin.
Immerse bovine tail in the diluted Betadine solution for 5 minutes.
Dry tail briefly with sterile gauze and place on sterile work station.
Remove muscle around tail carefully with scalpel blade #22.
Chop away unnecessary parts of the tail, typically both ends containing large and very small IVDs.
Trim remaining muscle and tendons around IVD using scalpel blade #10, being careful not to cut outer annulus.
Optionally mark anterior side of IVD with surgical skin marker.
Locate connection point between IVD and vertebra by gently moving the tail.
Feel border between IVD and bone using dull side of scalpel blade.
Place cleaving site 1-2 mm away from IVD towards vertebra.
Position custom-made industrial blade holder on the cleaving site.
Cleave IVD and vertebra by hammering on top of the custom-made industrial blade holder.
Repeat cleaving on the other side of the IVD-vertebra connection.
Wrap isolated IVD with sterile gauze moistened with 0.9% sodium chloride containing 55 mM sodium citrate.
Isolate additional IVDs to reach the desired sample number, typically around six discs with diameters between 10-20 mm.
Connect the jet lavage system with sterile Lactated Ringer's solution.
Hold the IVD with forceps and jet-lavage both sides of the endplate surface using Zimmer Pulsavac jet-lavage system.
Shoot the jet gun on the endplate surface at an angle between 30 - 60° for about 30 seconds on each side.
Place the IVD back into a 6-well plate and wrap with moistened gauze while preparing another disc sample.
IVDs are ready for organ culture and downstream applications such as cell viability, mechanical loading, or further culturing.
Prepare a 1% solution of procion red in PBS2.
Place the intervertebral disc in at least 100 mL of dye solution.
Allow the dye to diffuse into the IVD for 24 hours under free swelling conditions.
Flash-freeze the IVD in liquid nitrogen and thaw it back to room temperature.
Dehydrate the IVD by transferring it through acetone baths pre-cooled at -80°C, then -20°C, then 4°C, and finally at room temperature.
Embed the IVD in poly-methyl-acrylate (PMMA).
Cut PMMA-embedded IVD into 100 μm thick sections with a sharp blade.
View the sections using fluorescence microscopy to observe procion red fluorescence.
Measure disc height and overall integrity using histological sections stained with safranin O/fast green or Meyer's Hematoxilin.
Scan cell viability in 3D using confocal laser scanning microscope and live/dead staining kit.
